diagnostic_scope: Velocity-only first-step coast comparison with propeller child links rigidly merged into base_link

cg_offset_counterfactual.interpretation: The merged-body run already is the requested comX=0 test. Its response remained identical to articulated VRX, so the 7.54 mm base-link CG offset does not cause the first-step residual.

telemetry_comparison: All samples used for the first-step comparison and subsequent shared timestamps are numerically identical. The CSVs differ only at t=0.1 where articulated yaw rate is 3.74596e-16 versus 0, and because the articulated capture includes one additional t=5.3 sample.
conclusion: Rigidly merging the propeller child links and moving the aggregate CG exactly to the origin produces zero change in the measured response. Articulated-body coupling and CG-offset coupling are therefore both ruled out as causes of the Node/VRX first-step residual. Surface dynamics are also excluded from this isolated result because the Surface plugins were disabled in both runs. The next remaining diagnostic target is the planar-constraint reduction itself.
